items.title: An ending changes the kind of word

cells.note: The verb becomes a noun; this particular noun has its own meaning to learn.
The noun becomes a describing verb: affected by the thing the noun names.

items.caption: These endings change the word itself. The noun-making ending has both event-naming and learned-word jobs; the describing ending is different from a verb’s long-form ending.

items.title: Read the job of the prefix
items.caption: The counting prefix spreads a number over each one. The time prefixes place their words in past or future time; not every time word has a base that stands on its own.

items.title: A repeated piece makes this plural

states.label: One girl
states.note: The verb has no doubled piece and the noun carries *le*.

states.label: More than one girl
states.note: The second-to-last syllable is repeated, and the particular plural has no article in front.

items.caption: The doubled piece is the stressed syllable. Plurality is its most common job; the chapter asks you to recognize printed forms rather than build new plurals.

items.title: This small group goes the other way

states.label: One cat
states.note: The whole root is doubled in the singular.

states.label: More than one cat
states.note: The bare root is the plural here.

items.caption: This is a small closed group of colour and size words. The doubled form is singular in this pair, so doubling by itself does not always mean more than one.

items.title: Read the built word, not just its shape

data.question: What does this printed built word express?

prompts.why: This doubled word states repetition directly.
The doubled word has a learned meaning, swallowing with difficulty, rather than a plain again-and-again translation.
The prefix and ending together give the one-another reading.
The noun becomes a describing verb: affected by the dirt the noun names.

items.intro: Use the chapter’s meaning for the whole word; a visible piece does not settle every meaning.
